github-stars-heldout.label: Figure 1
github-stars-heldout.caption: Monthly GitHub star increments: observed history and forecasts from the last common rolling origin (August 2025). The vertical line separates training observations from the twelve evaluation months. Shading shows the nominal 80% SARIMA prediction interval; crosses mark observations outside it. Panels use logarithmic vertical scales. Only the last two training years are displayed.

npm-downloads-heldout.label: Figure 2
npm-downloads-heldout.caption: Monthly npm downloads in millions. SARIMA and persistence forecasts from August 2025 are shown against subsequent observations. Shading is the nominal 80% SARIMA prediction interval; axes are logarithmic. The cutoff and display window match Figure 1.

rmse-by-horizon.label: Table 2
rmse-by-horizon.caption: Lowest-RMSE family at each exact forecast horizon (24 origins).

rmse-12-months.label: Table 3
rmse-12-months.caption: Twelve-month rolling-origin RMSE. NPM values are millions of downloads; GitHub values are monthly stars.

intervals-12-months.label: Table 4
intervals-12-months.caption: Twelve-month diagnostics for the RMSE winner. Coverage and WAPE are percentages; width and interval score use millions for NPM and stars for GitHub.

residual-diagnostics.label: Table 5
residual-diagnostics.caption: Full-history Ljung–Box diagnostics from the saved fits. Lag is shared within each row; k is the SARIMA adjustment. ETS and Prophet use k=0 and exploratory p-values.

index-direction-classes.label: Table 6
index-direction-classes.caption: Year-on-year directions from September 2023 through August 2026. Each framework contributes 36 months.

index-weight-sensitivity.label: Figure 3
index-weight-sensitivity.caption: Year-on-year change in the geometric index. The line uses equal weights. Dots mark months when downloads and stars moved in opposite directions. Shading spans download weights from 0.25 to 0.75. Where the band crosses zero, the choice of weight determines the sign.

index-component-sarima-6-months.label: Figure 4
index-component-sarima-6-months.caption: Six-month-ahead forecasts of the equal-weight dynamics index, by target month. Each point forecast uses component SARIMA models fitted six months earlier. Shading spans the 10th to 90th percentiles of 4,000 paired bootstrap paths; crosses mark observations outside the nominal 80% prediction interval. Panel counts give coverage over 24 origins. Vertical scales are logarithmic.

index-route-comparison.label: Table 7
index-route-comparison.caption: Equal-weight index forecasts over 24 origins. Fit is the lowest-WAPE nonbaseline fit in each row (D: direct, C: components). Δ is its WAPE minus ordinary persistence WAPE. Family columns give component minus direct WAPE, in percentage points. Hits count correct annual directions for the selected fit, ordinary persistence (N) and last observed annual direction (L).

full-history-models.label: Table 8
full-history-models.caption: Selected full-history SARIMA and ETS structures and SARIMA innovation variance.

sarima-coefficients.label: Table 9
sarima-coefficients.caption: Full-history SARIMA coefficient estimates, standard errors (SE) and approximate conditional 95% Wald intervals.

index-react-point-errors.note: Equal-weight geometric index over 24 origins. D = direct index forecast; C = forecasts of the two components combined. MAE and RMSE use index points; WAPE is a percentage.

index-direction-accuracy.label: Table S20
index-direction-accuracy.caption: Exact matches of annual direction out of 24 forecasts. D denotes direct forecasts and C forecasts assembled from components. The level baselines give the same point predictions under either route. At twelve months both predict zero annual change. Table S20 scores up, down and unchanged separately.
index-direction-accuracy.note: Equal-weight geometric index over 24 origins. D = direct index forecast; C = forecasts of the two components combined.

index-weight-range.label: Figure S7
index-weight-range.caption: Number of opposing framework–month observations with a strict annual index direction throughout a symmetric weight interval. Width is 100(1-2a) percentage points. Labels give the download-weight bounds and the count. Each downward step occurs when an interval first includes a break-even weight.
